display_name: Dwarven (the Durn, three dialects of one tongue)
_note: The dwarven tier: one people (the Durn, 'the deep-folk') speaking one tongue, DURNKAD ('the deep-speech'), in three DIALECTS - not deep branches. DESIGN CONTRAST WITH THE ELVES: the elvish branches drifted far apart (each its own sound-law, its own sacred ending, each the deep ancestor of a human language cluster). The dwarves are insular, clannish, and fiercely traditional, so their speech barely drifts: the three dialects differ only by small allophony in the ROOT (Gormdurn hardens and geminates; Khraaldurn lengthens its vowels) and SHARE everything else - the same lexicon, the same titles, the same divine ending. Dwarven is a self-contained ISOLATE: it is NOT ancestral to any human family (unlike Vanethir). AESTHETIC (the sound): hard consonant frames (k/g/d/t/b/p, clusters dr/br/gr/kr/thr/rd/rg/rk/nd, geminates kk/gg/dd/mm/nn) around soft open vowels (a/o/u, some e/i); short, heavy CVC syllables with initial stress - rhythmic, like hammer-strokes on the anvil, the soft vowels rolling a lilt between the hard beats. Demihuman tier (race dwarf): golden-age->enclave arc, alignment weights per branch (catalog 5.2). DEITY names are morphs of the Agrippan canon, never real gods (no Tolkien/Norse/Warhammer dwarf-gods); they take the shared divine ending -drumm (m) / -drumma (f), the 'anvil-named' suffix - the hammer-beat by which the gods are honored.

branch_laws._note: SMALL drift only - these are dialects, not branches. The consonant skeleton and the whole word are shared; only minor allophony separates them, so a word is recognizably the same across all three.
branch_laws.khordurn: CENTRAL (the standard): hard frames + soft a/o/u; short CVC; clusters and geminates as written. The baseline against which the other two are measured.
branch_laws.gormdurn: FIRE-dialect: a slight hardening - final and medial stops geminate (-un -> -unn, -ak -> -akk), o tends to u; a crackling, clipped edge. Otherwise identical to Khordurn.
branch_laws.khraaldurn: FROST-dialect: a slight lengthening - root vowels draw out and round (-un -> -uun, a -> aa), final stops soften a touch; a slow, cold roll. Otherwise identical to Khordurn.

theonym_set._note: The 25-power canon as Dwarven forms (morphs of the Agrippan canon), each with the three DIALECT reflexes. Read across a row = the SAME word with tiny drift (dialects, not branches): Gormdurn geminates, Khraaldurn lengthens. DEITY names take the shared SACRED GENDERED ending -drumm (m) / -drumma (f) - the 'anvil-named' suffix - NOT the mortal endings or the bare common-noun root. Gender is read off the Agrippan canon: -us/-o/-um = masculine, -a/-ia = feminine; the One is supreme masculine. Representative set (the build assembles the full 25). The forge (Orlundrumm) and the mine/mountain (Gundundrumm) are the most-honored gods; the dead (Delrundrumm) underwrite the ancestor-cult.

_endings._note: THREE ending-classes keep gods, mortals, and common nouns distinct, and (unlike the elves) the divine ending is SHARED across all three dialects - dwarven drifts too little to split it. (1) DIVINE = -drumm (m) / -drumma (f), the anvil-named suffix, NO parentage sense. (2) mortal personal = -un/-ar/-ok (m), -a/-na/-ra (f), with clan-lineage (Kron [X]) and an optional patronymic -kun (son of) / -ketta (daughter of). (3) common-noun/place = the bare nominal root (-un/-ar/-ak/-grund).
_endings.dialect_note: all three dialects share -drumm/-drumma; the drift shows only in the root (Gormdurn geminates, Khraaldurn lengthens).

proto_roots._note: Dwarven core-concept roots (hard frame, soft vowel, short), shared across the three dialects with only the small drift (Gormdurn geminates, Khraaldurn lengthens). Realized per culture's lexicon.

title_skeleton._note: ACKS 7 tiers; one ladder, three near-identical dialect reflexes (small drift). Dwarven realms are ancient vault-kingdoms (golden-age, now mostly fallen to fastness-holds); civ government with clan-based nobility.

dwarf_canon._alignment_note: Dwarves lean Neutral across the board (setting-lore 5.2 #51-53). Khordurn the most law-touched (the orderly vault-kingdoms); Gormdurn the most chaos-touched (the fire-cult, human sacrifice); Khraaldurn the most purely Neutral (the hard, withdrawn frost-holds). Each kit's alignment_allowed lists the seed/shift options; these weights set the dominant seed.
dwarf_canon.lifecycle: high peak_strength, high collapse_proneness, end_state enclave (golden-age vault-kingdoms -> hard collapse to fastness-holds; dwarves are strong domain-builders, so their fallen holds are deep and ruin-rich).
dwarf_canon.seed_biomes: Khordurn any mountain EXCEPT glacial and volcanic; Gormdurn volcanic mountain only; Khraaldurn glacial mountains or tundra hills only.
dwarf_canon.conquest: in-biome genocide, out-of-biome vassalize, always-genocide vs other demihumans (catalog 5.2).
dwarf_canon.religion: ANCESTOR-CENTRIC: daily liturgy and prayer go to the honored dead (the durnad) and clan-fathers (fadrun) at the tomb-hall; the gods are honored at yearly/seasonal FESTIVALS, foremost the forge (Orlundrumm) and the mine/mountain (Gundundrumm) - the powers of fire and earth. The Gormdurn (volcanic) lean hardest into fire: Marakadrumm the forge-fire, with human sacrifice cast into the volcanoes.

conventions.people_name_default: MORTAL naming: a hard-soft-short given name (m -un/-ar/-ok, f -a/-na/-ra) + the clan (Kron [X]); dwarves identify by clan and forefather, with an optional patronymic -kun (son of) / -ketta (daughter of). A mortal named FOR a Power uses the power's ROOT + a mortal ending (Orlun+ar = Orlunar, a smith named for the forge-god), never the divine -drumm/-drumma (which belongs to the Power alone).
conventions.transparent_vs_opaque: high; dwarves are literal and traditional - most names transparently name stone, forge, clan, or ancestor.
